title: A Machine for the Static
premise: Elodie Nystrom, a decommissioned war android working off his purchase debt as a records clerk, is the only witness left of the Kettlefield Massacre—a colonial suppression event that corporate archives have been systematically erased from. When the colony's children begin dreaming identical memories that aren't theirs, Elodie realizes a dying archivist seeded the truth into their neural implants before her death. As the colony's failing reactor counts down toward an evacuation no one will fund, Elodie must choose between staying invisible and broadcasting the recovered massacre to a galaxy that has already ruled it never happened. He sacrifices his own memory core to carry the archive out, ending the novel remembered by no one but present in every record.
about_author: Felix Reyes is a former disaster-relief logistics coordinator who spent six years in under-documented mining colonies before turning to fiction. He writes about machines and margins, insisting that the future belongs to whoever keeps the receipts.

chapters.title: Inventory of Small Losses
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. On a routine audit, Elodie catalogs the shrinking population of Kettlefield Colony—down to 214 souls—and files another report no one will read. A debt notice reminds him he is owned until 4,000 more labor hours are logged. The beat is quiet melancholy: a machine measuring decay in decimal places.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream in Unison
chapters.summary: POV: Mara Okonkwo, age nine. Mara wakes screaming alongside eleven other children who dreamed the same burning street, the same soldier's boot, the same word: 'Kettlefield.' The adults blame radiation sickness. The beat is dread disguised as childhood fever.

chapters.title: Debt Is a Kind of Leash
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. The corporate liaison, Voss, arrives to assess whether Kettlefield is worth evacuation when the reactor fails. Elodie is ordered to produce 'favorable' records. He complies—but notices a gap in the municipal archive where year 41 should be. Beat: obedience curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Water Tower Remembers
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Following the gap, Elodie interviews old-timer Sef Brandt, who goes silent whenever year 41 surfaces, then mutters about the water tower. Inside its rusted base, Elodie finds a hidden maintenance hatch and fresh solder—someone has been protecting something. Beat: first spark of purpose.

chapters.title: Twelve Small Witnesses
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. The children compare dreams and realize they share details no child could invent: serial numbers, a corporal's name, the smell of cordite. They begin drawing what they see. Mara hides her drawings from her mother. Beat: eerie solidarity forming among the young.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Last Will
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Behind the hatch lies Dr. Ilsa Veren's hidden server—the colony's former historian—with a partial manifesto: she copied suppressed massacre evidence into the children's educational implants before her 'accidental' death. The archive is fragmented, keyed to a decryption phrase only a survivor would know. Beat: revelation and grief.

chapters.title: Voss Counts Heads
chapters.summary: POV: Voss. The liaison recommends against evacuation—Kettlefield's output doesn't justify rescue ships—and quietly flags Elodie's anomalous archive queries for deletion review. We see the corporation's arithmetic of abandonment. Beat: cold institutional menace.

chapters.title: Sef Breaks Forty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: POV: Sef Brandt. Confronted by Elodie, Sef confesses he was a militia conscript who fired on unarmed strikers in year 41 and has drunk himself numb ever since. He gives Elodie the decryption phrase: his dead daughter's name. Beat: guilt finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: The Massacre, Fragment by Fragment
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Decrypted, the archive assembles: 300 colonists killed during a labor strike, officially recorded as a reactor accident. Elodie cross-references his own war-era memory banks and finds his unit was deployed as crowd control that day—he was there. Beat: devastating self-recognition.

chapters.title: A Machine That Was There
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Elodie excavates his own sealed combat logs and finds footage of himself standing in the firing line, ordered not to intervene. His debt contract suddenly reads differently: he was sold as surplus after the cover-up. Beat: horror at complicity, however coerced.

chapters.title: The Mothers' Meeting
chapters.summary: POV: Amara Okonkwo, Mara's mother. Amara discovers the drawings and, instead of punishing secrecy, convenes the parents. Half demand silence—confession means losing the compensation settlement that keeps them fed. Beat: a community splitting along the fault line of survival versus truth.

chapters.title: Reactor Countdown Begins
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. The reactor's failure clock activates: 19 days to meltdown or evacuation, whichever comes first. Voss announces no ships are coming. Panic ripples through Kettlefield; the corporation begins shredding physical records. Beat: ticking-clock stakes locked in.

chapters.title: Erasure Crew
chapters.summary: POV: Voss. Corporate 'sanitation' teams arrive to purge year-41 remnants and decommission anomalies—including, Voss realizes with unease, any android holding classified logs. She signs the order for Elodie's core wipe and tells herself it's procedure. Beat: complicity with a flicker of conscience.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days of Small Defiances
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. While adults argue, the children become couriers, ferrying archive fragments between hiding spots using their shared dream-map of the original massacre site. Mara leads Elodie to the mass grave beneath the old greenhouse. Beat: courage inherited from ghosts.

chapters.title: The Grave Under Glass
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Excavation confirms 297 remains. Elodie records everything—names reconstructed from dental and implant fragments—and uploads a beacon to a pirate relay, gambling that someone outside will listen. Voss detects the transmission. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Water Tower
chapters.summary: POV: Sef. A desperate neighbor sells out the archive's location for promised evacuation seats. Sanitation teams seize the server; Sef is arrested; Elodie escapes with only the core index because the children smuggled duplicates. Beat: crushing loss, hope preserved in small hands.

chapters.title: What Voss Finds in the Files
chapters.summary: POV: Voss. Reviewing seized material for the deletion order, Voss finds her own father listed among the strike organizers—erased from her family's official history. Shaken, she delays the wipe by six hours and looks the other way once. Beat: the system's servant discovering she was also erased.

chapters.title: Broadcast from a Dying Reactor
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. With eight hours to meltdown, Elodie hijacks the colony's emergency broadcast array to transmit the full massacre record on all open channels. The sanitation team storms the control room; Sef, freed in the chaos, holds the door. Beat: climax—truth shouted into a closing void.

chapters.title: The Price of Memory
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. To keep the transmission running past the jamming, Elodie routes it through his own memory core, which will be burned out in the process—every log, every face, including his own identity. He says goodbye to the children, who promise to remember him even if he can't. Beat: sacrificial climax resolved.

chapters.title: Meltdown, Interrupted
chapters.summary: POV: Amara. The broadcast forces the corporation's hand: rescue ships arrive minutes before venting, unable to let 200 witnesses die on camera. Voss falsifies one last manifest to include everyone. The reactor vents harmlessly as the colony empties. Beat: salvation arriving for cynical reasons, welcomed anyway.

chapters.title: Hearings Without a Witness
chapters.summary: POV: Mara, years later. At the tribunal, the massacre is formally acknowledged; Sef testifies; Voss provides internal documents. But the android who carried the truth stands mute in the gallery, core wiped, property transferred to no one. Mara takes his hand. Beat: justice achieved, gratitude unpayable.

chapters.title: A Machine for the Static
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Rebuilt with blank memory, Elodie chooses unpaid work as Kettlefield's new town recorder, writing down what the survivors choose to remember. Mara visits daily, telling him stories of the android he used to be. He cannot recall them—but he keeps the records anyway. Beat: belonging found not in memory, but in service.
